system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Wattlebridge Holdings | Project Kestrel**

The Seller’s assertions of “market standard”, principal-level agreement and “FINAL” status are not evidence of Buyer approval. The positions below are proposed Buyer negotiating asks, based on the extracts supplied—not verification of the underlying DD documents.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general cap; propose **50% / AUD 12m**, with separate protection for excluded categories. | **Counter at 50%**, reserving category carve-outs — 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible** basket. | Lower thresholds; propose **AUD 10,000 de minimis / AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated. | **Counter and exclude special categories from thresholds** — the proposed combination eliminates smaller claims and permanently absorbs the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, separate category periods, and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Seek 36 months; reject blanket application** — latent issues may emerge after 18 months and require longer to quantify. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and deadline. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, all issued shares and freedom from encumbrances; **100% price cap**, no thresholds and a longer period, proposed **seven years**. | **Reject general-regime treatment** — Buyer must have meaningful recourse if Seller cannot transfer the ownership purchased. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception identified. | Express protection for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, including attribution to Seller of relevant representatives’ conduct; preservation of non-excludable rights. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual deadlines, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions** — contractual protections must not shield fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, against relevant warranties, in an agreed frozen disclosure set. | **Reject blanket and constructive disclosure** — document availability alone does not adequately identify the risk Buyer is accepting. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without deemed knowledge or inquiry duty. | **Reject discoverability and adviser imputation; preserve specific indemnities** — diligence should not transfer undiscovered Seller risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by written consent, although final consent and satisfaction of associated conditions are absent. | A non-waivable-by-Seller completion condition requiring effective consent, satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions and no unacceptable contract changes. | **Require evidence before Completion, with Buyer-controlled waiver and long-stop termination rights** — approximately 30% of revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release after Completion. | Binding payout figures, repayment at Completion and effective releases of all relevant security and guarantees through an agreed simultaneous process. | **Reject an unsecured post-Completion promise; deduct debt once in the price/funds flow** — Buyer should receive the agreed debt-free business without inherited security exposure. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller economic responsibility for transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with conditions and payment timing verified. | **Itemise and fund through a price deduction, retention or direct payment, without double counting** — omission otherwise makes Buyer bear transaction-related remuneration. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** remains recorded as open, without proof of payment or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective ownership/assignment of relevant IP before Completion; broader indemnity for ownership defects, third-party claims and remediation costs. | **Require documentary cure plus a standalone indemnity outside general limitations** — paying an invoice alone may not establish the IP rights Buyer needs. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legal notification assessment, updates and protection against pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation/remediation covenants and a tailored indemnity, with completion protection if findings are material** — uncertainty is neither proof of a notifiable breach nor evidence of immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, timing, scope, cancellation rights, accruals and benefit to the post-Completion business. | **Reserve treatment pending DD; require consent for new commitments and price protection where justified** — neither ordinary-course status nor debt-like treatment is established. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend across all Claims. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price adjustments, debt/payment obligations and fraud. | **Create an explicit category-by-category limitations matrix** — blanket wording could neutralise negotiated protections or restrict recovery of the purchase-price adjustment itself. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register is relied upon as evidence of Seller’s 100% ownership. | Reconcile the register with corporate records, issue/transfer history, certificates, options and other rights; check encumbrances and obtain completion transfers and releases. | **Verify independently and retain full title warranties** — a register entry alone does not resolve every ownership, dilution or security risk. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion liabilities with agreed exclusions, a longer period—proposed seven years with assessment extensions—and tailored IP warranties and survival. | **Keep both expressly open; negotiate separate caps, periods and indemnity treatment** — tax can surface late and IP ownership is central to the value of a SaaS business. |

**Priority completion protections:** Bluefen consent and its conditions, Riverlark repayment/releases, Ironquay ownership cure, and a corrected funds flow. Known disclosed risks should receive express contractual protection rather than reliance solely on warranties that disclosure may qualify.
=== END ADVICE ===
